# 3. Did EBP/CDEP services impact clinical and functional outcomes for clients who participated?

The Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) is a brief behavioral screening questionnaire about 2-17 year-olds. It exists in several versions; four are used here: P2-4, P4-10, P11-17, and S11-17.

- **3.11:** To what extent did parents/caregivers report reductions in disruptive behaviors after receiving the intervention? Uses the externalizing score (sum of the conduct and hyperactivity scales).
- **3.16:** To what extent did children/youth report improvements in coping/handling overall difficulties after the intervention? Uses the total difficulties score.

**Inclusion criteria:** 1. must have initial time point data (i.e., be enrolled in an intervention); 2. must have a valid assessment collected at both initial and discharge comparison time points.

**Scoring:** An **increase** in score indicates a negative outcome. Published cut-points are available for both the total score and the sub-scales. Valid assessment: cases with a total of more than one missing value on all SDQ items are excluded.

**Assumptions:** The cleaned files (from `data cleaning/sdq_data_cleaning.qmd`) already exclude dates before 2024-01-01 and after the run date, exclude follow-ups within 3 days of the initial assessment, and pair each initial assessment to the LAST follow-up. Rows with no outcome recorded are left out before percentages are computed.

**Still to do for the final report (not yet in this script):** percent of clients within the 0-80, 81-90, and >90 percentile bands at initial and discharge for each of the four versions, a Sankey diagram of movement between bands, and a regression with SDQ score as the outcome and the 3.01 predictors.

```{r}
#| label: helpers
# Formatting, suppression, and table helpers are copied verbatim from the 1.01 script; keep them in sync.
fmt_n <- function(n) formatC(as.numeric(n), format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")
fmt_n_qa <- function(n) {
  ifelse(SHAREABLE & !is.na(n) & n > 0 & n < SUPPRESS_N, paste0("<", SUPPRESS_N), fmt_n(n))
}
fmt_pct <- function(p, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(p) | is.nan(p), "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * p))
}
fmt_p   <- function(p) case_when(is.na(p) ~ NA_character_, p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001", TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p))

# ---- Primary and complementary suppression ----
# `x` holds every published or derivable number in a table (cells and totals). Each element of `lines`
# indexes entries tied by one additive constraint, with the total LAST (a row's cells, then its total).
# Counts of 1 to k - 1 are suppressed, then more entries are suppressed until:
#   (a) no line has exactly one suppressed entry, which subtraction would recover;
#   (b) in a line whose total is shown, the suppressed cells add up to at least k, so their combined
#       count (total minus the shown cells) is not itself a small count; and
#   (c) no suppressed count below k, and no sum of two suppressed counts that is below k, can be
#       solved for exactly from all of the table's constraints taken together (checked by matrix rank).
# Extra suppressions go to the entry with the lowest `weight` (by default, the smallest count).
# An entry with weight Inf is never chosen, e.g. because another table already shows it. An entry
# that can be read off a line whose other entries are all zero or shown elsewhere cannot be
# protected, so it is never chosen either. If no entry can protect a hidden count, the render stops
# rather than publish a count that could be recovered.
pick_entry <- function(cand, weight) {
  cand <- cand[is.finite(weight[cand])]
  if (length(cand) == 0L) NA_integer_ else cand[which.min(weight[cand])]
}

recoverable_entries <- function(x, lines, s, k) {
  sup <- which(s)
  if (length(sup) == 0L) return(integer())
  A <- do.call(rbind, lapply(lines, function(ln) {
    row <- numeric(length(x))
    row[ln] <- c(rep(1, length(ln) - 1L), -1)
    row[sup]
  }))
  A <- A[rowSums(A != 0) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(A) == 0L) return(integer())
  r <- qr(A)$rank
  solvable <- function(v) qr(rbind(A, v))$rank == r
  unit <- function(j) as.numeric(seq_along(sup) == j)
  small <- which(x[sup] < k)
  hits <- sup[small[vapply(small, function(j) solvable(unit(j)), logical(1))]]
  if (length(hits) == 0L && length(small) > 1L) {
    for (pr in combn(small, 2, simplify = FALSE)) {
      if (sum(x[sup[pr]]) < k && solvable(unit(pr[1]) + unit(pr[2]))) {
        hits <- sup[pr]
        break
      }
    }
  }
  hits
}

suppress_lines <- function(x, lines, k = SUPPRESS_N, init = NULL, weight = x) {
  s <- !is.na(x) & x > 0 & x < k
  if (!is.null(init)) s <- s | init
  repeat {
    pinned <- unlist(lapply(lines, function(ln) {
      unknown <- ln[x[ln] > 0 & (is.finite(weight[ln]) | s[ln])]
      if (length(unknown) == 1L && is.finite(weight[unknown])) unknown
    }))
    if (length(pinned) == 0L) break
    weight[pinned] <- Inf
  }
  open_entries <- function(idx) idx[!s[idx] & x[idx] > 0]
  cannot_protect <- function() {
    stop("Complementary suppression cannot protect a hidden count: every entry that could be ",
         "hidden with it is zero or shown in another table.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  repeat {
    j <- NA_integer_
    for (ln in lines) {
      tot <- ln[length(ln)]
      cells <- ln[-length(ln)]
      small_sum <- !s[tot] && any(s[cells]) && sum(x[cells][s[cells]]) < k
      if (sum(s[ln]) == 1L || small_sum) {
        j <- pick_entry(open_entries(ln), weight)
        if (is.na(j)) cannot_protect()
        break
      }
    }
    if (is.na(j)) {
      rec <- recoverable_entries(x, lines, s, k)
      if (length(rec) > 0L) {
        near <- unique(unlist(lines[vapply(lines, function(ln) any(rec %in% ln), logical(1))]))
        j <- pick_entry(open_entries(near), weight)
        if (is.na(j)) j <- pick_entry(open_entries(seq_along(x)), weight)
        if (is.na(j)) cannot_protect()
      }
    }
    if (is.na(j)) break
    s[j] <- TRUE
  }
  s
}

# Suppression pattern for a matrix of counts with its totals attached: row totals in the last column
# and column totals in the last row. Every row and column is a line. Extra suppressions go to inner
# cells first, then to row totals, and to the grand total last, because hiding the grand total forces
# a column total to be hidden too. `init` marks entries that start hidden and `fixed` marks entries
# that are never hidden, usually because another table hides or shows the same number.
suppress_table <- function(ext, init = FALSE, fixed = FALSE) {
  R <- nrow(ext) - 1L
  C <- ncol(ext) - 1L
  idx <- matrix(seq_along(ext), nrow(ext))
  lines <- c(lapply(seq_len(R + 1L), function(i) idx[i, ]),
             lapply(seq_len(C + 1L), function(j) idx[, j]))
  weight <- as.vector(ext)
  weight[idx[seq_len(R), C + 1L]] <- weight[idx[seq_len(R), C + 1L]] + 1e9
  weight[idx[R + 1L, C + 1L]] <- weight[idx[R + 1L, C + 1L]] + 2e9
  weight[rep_len(as.vector(fixed), length(ext))] <- Inf
  s <- suppress_lines(as.vector(ext), lines, init = rep_len(as.vector(init), length(ext)), weight = weight)
  matrix(s, nrow(ext))
}

# One-way frequency table in the interim report's layout: N, % of all, and % excluding N/As.
# `not_reported` lists labels (besides NA) that count as non-substantive. The result carries the
# categories it shows and hides, so a cross-tab of the same variable can match them (see `like`).
tab_one_way <- function(x, label = "Category", order = character(), not_reported = character(),
                        show_valid = TRUE, digits = 1) {
  if (length(x) == 0L) return(tibble(!!label := "No records"))
  x <- if_else(is.na(x), NOT_REPORTED, as.character(x))
  nr_labels <- c(not_reported, NOT_REPORTED)
  counts <- count(tibble(category = x), category)
  present <- counts$category
  lv <- c(intersect(setdiff(order, nr_labels), present),
          sort(setdiff(present, c(order, nr_labels))),
          intersect(nr_labels, present))
  counts <- counts[match(lv, counts$category), ]

  n <- counts$n
  is_sub <- !(counts$category %in% nr_labels)
  m <- length(n)
  i_sub <- m + 1L; i_nr <- m + 2L; i_tot <- m + 3L
  x_all <- c(n, sum(n[is_sub]), sum(n[!is_sub]), sum(n))
  lines <- list(c(which(is_sub), i_sub), c(which(!is_sub), i_nr), c(i_sub, i_nr, i_tot))
  s <- if (SHAREABLE) suppress_lines(x_all, lines) else rep(FALSE, length(x_all))
  sc <- s[seq_len(m)]

  body <- tibble(
    category = counts$category,
    N = if_else(sc, SUPPR, fmt_n(n)),
    `%` = if_else(sc | s[i_tot], SUPPR, fmt_pct(n / x_all[i_tot], digits)),
    `% (excluding N/As)` = case_when(
      !is_sub         ~ "N/A",
      sc | s[i_sub]   ~ SUPPR,
      TRUE            ~ fmt_pct(n / x_all[i_sub], digits)
    )
  )
  subtotal <- tibble(
    category = "Subtotal: substantive responses",
    N = if_else(s[i_sub], SUPPR, fmt_n(x_all[i_sub])),
    `%` = if_else(s[i_sub] | s[i_tot], SUPPR, fmt_pct(x_all[i_sub] / x_all[i_tot], digits)),
    `% (excluding N/As)` = if_else(s[i_sub], SUPPR, "100.0%")
  )
  total <- tibble(category = "Total", N = if_else(s[i_tot], SUPPR, fmt_n(x_all[i_tot])),
                  `%` = if_else(s[i_tot], SUPPR, "100.0%"), `% (excluding N/As)` = "")

  out <- if (show_valid) {
    bind_rows(body[is_sub, ], subtotal, body[!is_sub, ], total)
  } else {
    bind_rows(body, total) |> select(-`% (excluding N/As)`)
  }
  out <- rename(out, !!label := category)
  attr(out, "hidden") <- counts$category[sc]
  attr(out, "shown")  <- counts$category[!sc]
  # A cross-tab of this variable leaves out missing values, so its grand total can be read from this
  # table only when no total and no non-substantive count here is hidden.
  attr(out, "total_hidden") <- any(s[c(which(!is_sub), i_sub, i_nr, i_tot)])
  out
}

# Two-way table with row percentages and counts, e.g. "45% (1,234)", plus a Total row and an N column.
# Every row and column (including the Total row and N column) is a suppression line (see
# `suppress_table()`). A row whose total is hidden shows counts without percentages, because its
# percentages would reveal that total. Rows follow factor level order when `rows` is a factor.
# `like`: an earlier table of the same column variable over the same clients (one-way or two-way).
# Its hidden categories and grand total start hidden in this table's Total row, and the ones it shows
# are never hidden here, so the two tables cannot be combined to recover a suppressed count.
tab_two_way <- function(rows, cols, row_label = "Group", col_order = character(), digits = 0,
                        like = NULL) {
  if (length(rows) == 0L) return(tibble(!!row_label := "No records"))
  row_lv <- as.character(sort(unique(rows[!is.na(rows)])))
  rows <- if_else(is.na(rows), NOT_REPORTED, as.character(rows))
  cols <- if_else(is.na(cols), NOT_REPORTED, as.character(cols))
  if (any(rows == NOT_REPORTED)) row_lv <- c(row_lv, NOT_REPORTED)
  present <- unique(cols)
  col_lv <- c(intersect(setdiff(col_order, NOT_REPORTED), present),
              sort(setdiff(present, c(col_order, NOT_REPORTED))),
              intersect(NOT_REPORTED, present))

  m <- unclass(table(factor(rows, row_lv), factor(cols, col_lv)))
  R <- nrow(m); C <- ncol(m)
  ext <- rbind(cbind(m, rowSums(m)), c(colSums(m), sum(m)))

  s_mat <- matrix(FALSE, R + 1, C + 1)
  if (SHAREABLE) {
    init <- fixed <- matrix(FALSE, R + 1, C + 1)
    if (!is.null(like)) {
      init[R + 1, ]  <- c(col_lv %in% attr(like, "hidden"), isTRUE(attr(like, "total_hidden")))
      fixed[R + 1, ] <- c(col_lv %in% attr(like, "shown"), !init[R + 1, C + 1])
    }
    s_mat <- suppress_table(ext, init, fixed)
  }
  shown_s <- s_mat
  if (SHAREABLE) {
    # In a row or column whose total is below k, zeros are hidden too: otherwise they would show
    # which categories the small group falls into (e.g., a row that is zero everywhere but one cell).
    small_row <- ext[, C + 1] > 0 & ext[, C + 1] < SUPPRESS_N
    small_col <- ext[R + 1, ] > 0 & ext[R + 1, ] < SUPPRESS_N
    shown_s <- s_mat | (ext == 0 & (outer(small_row, rep(TRUE, C + 1)) | outer(rep(TRUE, R + 1), small_col)))
  }

  pct <- ext / ext[, C + 1]
  cell <- matrix(paste0(fmt_pct(pct, digits), " (", fmt_n(ext), ")"), nrow(ext))
  no_pct <- s_mat[, C + 1]                      # rows (including Total) whose total is hidden
  cell[no_pct, ] <- matrix(fmt_n(ext[no_pct, , drop = FALSE]), sum(no_pct))
  cell[shown_s] <- SUPPR
  cell[, C + 1] <- ifelse(s_mat[, C + 1], SUPPR, fmt_n(ext[, C + 1]))
  colnames(cell) <- c(col_lv, "N")
  out <- as_tibble(cell) |> mutate(!!row_label := c(row_lv, "Total"), .before = 1)
  attr(out, "hidden") <- union(attr(like, "hidden"), col_lv[s_mat[R + 1, seq_len(C)]])
  attr(out, "shown")  <- col_lv[!s_mat[R + 1, seq_len(C)]]
  attr(out, "total_hidden") <- s_mat[R + 1, C + 1]
  out
}

# Show a table and keep a copy for the CSV export at the end.
EXPORT <- list()
show_table <- function(tbl, id, caption = NULL) {
  EXPORT[[id]] <<- tbl
  kable(tbl, caption = caption, align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(tbl) - 1)))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: outcome-helpers
# ---- Helpers shared by the 3.03 to 3.16 outcome scripts; keep them in sync ----
fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(as.numeric(x), format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")

data_path <- function(file) file.path(cfg$data_dir, file)
read_pairs <- function(file) read_csv(data_path(file), show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)

qa_flow <- tibble(step = character(), n = integer())
qa_add <- function(step, n) qa_flow <<- bind_rows(qa_flow, tibble(step = step, n = as.integer(n)))
is_small <- function(n) SHAREABLE & n > 0 & n < SUPPRESS_N

# Complete pairs in long form: one row per client and time point. `cols` names the initial and
# follow-up score columns, in that order.
scores_long <- function(d, cols = SCORE_COLS) {
  d |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(!is.na(client_system_id), if_all(all_of(cols), ~ !is.na(.x))) |>
    select(client_system_id, all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(cols), names_to = "score_type", values_to = "score_value") |>
    mutate(score_type = factor(TIMEPOINTS[match(score_type, cols)], levels = TIMEPOINTS))
}

# Mean, median, and SD at each time point (within each level of `by`, if given).
score_stats <- function(long, by = NULL) {
  long |>
    summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(score_value), median = median(score_value), sd = sd(score_value),
              .by = all_of(c(by, "score_type"))) |>
    arrange(across(all_of(c(by, "score_type"))))
}

# Shareable render: statistics for 1 to SUPPRESS_N - 1 clients are suppressed.
fmt_score_stats <- function(stats) {
  hide <- is_small(stats$n)
  stats |>
    mutate(across(c(mean, median, sd), ~ if_else(hide, SUPPR, fmt_num(.x))),
           n = if_else(hide, SUPPR, fmt_n(n))) |>
    rename(`Time point` = score_type, N = n, Mean = mean, Median = median, SD = sd)
}

# Clients by outcome, among clients with an outcome recorded.
tab_outcome <- function(x, label = "Outcome", order = character()) {
  tab_one_way(x[!is.na(x)], label, order, show_valid = FALSE)
}

# Clients scoring at or above `cut` at each time point. Shareable render: the count at or above, the
# count below, and the total are one suppression line, so a percentage is hidden with its count.
at_or_above <- function(long, cut) {
  long |>
    summarise(n = n(), n_at = sum(score_value >= cut), .by = score_type) |>
    mutate(s = map2(n_at, n, \(a, t) if (SHAREABLE) suppress_lines(c(a, t - a, t), list(1:3)) else rep(FALSE, 3)),
           hide_pct = map_lgl(s, \(s) any(s[1:2])), hide_n = map_lgl(s, 3), pct = n_at / n) |>
    select(-s)
}
fmt_at_or_above <- function(x, cut) {
  x |>
    transmute(`Time point` = score_type, N = if_else(hide_n, SUPPR, fmt_n(n)),
              !!paste0("% scoring ", cut, " or higher") := if_else(hide_pct, SUPPR, fmt_pct(pct)))
}

# ---- Figures ----
theme_scores <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 9), axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
          axis.line.x = element_line(color = "lightgrey", linewidth = 0.5),
          legend.title = element_blank(), legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 11), plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5))
}

# Print a figure and save a copy. A figure that draws counts or one mark per client could reveal a
# small count, so it is `internal_only` and a shareable render leaves it out. `make` is a function,
# so nothing is drawn in that case.
show_plot <- function(make, id, internal_only = FALSE, width = 7, height = 4.5) {
  if (!SHOW_FIGURES) return(invisible())
  if (internal_only && SHAREABLE) {
    cat("\n\n*Figure not shown in this shareable render: it could reveal a count below ", SUPPRESS_N, ".*\n\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  p <- make()
  ggsave(file.path(cfg$output_dir, paste0(FILE_TAG, "_", id, "_", RUN_MODE, ".png")), p,
         width = width, height = height, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  print(p)
  cat("\n\n")
}

plot_score_bars <- function(long, x_label, title) {
  ggplot(long, aes(score_value, fill = score_type)) +
    geom_bar(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single", padding = 0.01), width = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = TIMEPOINT_COLOURS) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = "Count", title = title) +
    theme_scores()
}

# Score distributions at the two time points, with a dotted line at each median.
plot_score_density <- function(long, x_label, title) {
  medians <- score_stats(long)
  ggplot(long, aes(score_value, fill = score_type, colour = score_type)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median, colour = score_type), medians, linetype = "dotted", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = TIMEPOINT_COLOURS, aesthetics = c("fill", "colour"),
                      labels = paste0(TIMEPOINTS, " (median = ", fmt_num(medians$median, 1), ")")) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_scores() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left")
}
# A shareable render draws score distributions only when every group has at least SUPPRESS_N clients.
any_small <- function(long, by = NULL) any(is_small(score_stats(long, by)$n))
```

```{r}
#| label: sdq-helpers
# ---- SDQ ----
# Quarter labels ("Q1 2025") as a factor in date order; as text they would sort alphabetically.
quarter_factor <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  lv <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])
  key <- str_match(lv, "Q(\\d)\\D+(\\d{4})")
  factor(x, levels = lv[order(as.integer(key[, 3]), as.integer(key[, 2]), lv)])
}

# Ridgelines by SDQ version (with a line at each median), beside the mean change (follow-up minus initial) for each version.
plot_sdq <- function(long, x_label, title) {
  long <- mutate(long, version = fct_drop(version))
  diffs <- score_stats(long, "version") |>
    select(version, score_type, mean) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = score_type, values_from = mean) |>
    mutate(difference = .data[[TIMEPOINTS[2]]] - .data[[TIMEPOINTS[1]]])
  gap <- ggplot(diffs, aes(1, version)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = fmt_num(difference)), size = 3, hjust = 0) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.15, 1.2))) +
    labs(title = "Mean difference\n(follow-up - initial);\na decrease is a\npositive outcome") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8))
  ridges <- ggplot(long, aes(score_value, version, fill = score_type, colour = score_type)) +
    geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.7, scale = 1.2, rel_min_height = 0.01, quantile_lines = TRUE, quantiles = 2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = TIMEPOINT_COLOURS, aesthetics = c("fill", "colour")) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.15, 1.2))) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_scores() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left")
  (ridges | gap) + plot_layout(widths = c(5, 1))
}

# One SDQ score (externalizing or total difficulties): outcome tables for each version, then the
# score statistics and distributions for all versions together.
sdq_score <- function(score, sq, title, initial, follow_up, outcome) {
  cat("\n\n## ", sq, " SDQ ", str_to_lower(title), "\n\n", sep = "")
  long <- pmap_dfr(SDQ_VERSIONS, function(id, version, file) {
    d <- sdq[[id]]
    key <- paste0("sdq_", id, "_", score)
    version_long <- scores_long(d, c(initial, follow_up))
    qa_add(paste0("SDQ ", version, ", ", str_to_lower(title), ": clients with both scores"),
           n_distinct(version_long$client_system_id))
    qa_add(paste0("SDQ ", version, ", ", str_to_lower(title), ": rows with no outcome recorded"), sum(is.na(d[[outcome]])))

    cat("\n\n### ", version, "\n\n", sep = "")
    overall <- tab_outcome(d[[outcome]], "Positive outcome")
    show_table(overall, paste0(key, "_outcome"),
               caption = "Clients by outcome (a lower follow-up score is a positive outcome)") |> print()
    if (BY_QUARTER) {
      dq <- filter(d, !is.na(.data[[outcome]]))
      tab_two_way(quarter_factor(dq$follow_up_quarter), dq[[outcome]], "Follow-up quarter", like = overall) |>
        show_table(paste0(key, "_outcome_by_quarter"), caption = "Outcome by follow-up quarter") |> print()
    }
    mutate(version_long, version = factor(version, SDQ_VERSIONS$version))
  })

  cat("\n\n### Scores at each time point, by version\n\n")
  fmt_score_stats(score_stats(long, "version")) |>
    rename(Version = version) |>
    show_table(paste0("sdq_", score, "_stats")) |> print()
  show_plot(\() plot_sdq(long, paste("SDQ", str_to_lower(title)),
                         paste0("Distribution of initial and follow-up scores by version, SDQ ", str_to_lower(title))),
            paste0("sdq_", score, "_ridgeline"), internal_only = any_small(long, "version"), width = 9, height = 6)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: load_sdq
sdq <- map(set_names(SDQ_VERSIONS$file, SDQ_VERSIONS$id), read_pairs)
iwalk(sdq, \(d, id) qa_add(paste0("SDQ ", id, " file: rows read"), nrow(d)))
```

```{r}
#| label: sdq
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
pwalk(SDQ_SCORES, sdq_score)
```

## Scoring reference: reductions in disruptive behaviors (3.11)

### 2-4 (Provider)

**'Internalising' and 'externalising' scores**: The internalising score
ranges from 0 to 20 and is the sum of the emotional and peer
difficulties scales. The externalising score ranges from 0 to 20 and is
the sum of the conduct and hyperactivity scales. We will be using the
externalising score for this KPI.

**Calculation:** Hyperactivity scale (2, 10, 15, 21, 25) + conduct scale
(5, 7, 12, 18, 22) Cut off bands

## Scoring reference: improvements in coping and handling overall difficulties (3.16)

### 2-4 (Provider)

**Scoring:** In most respects, the 2-4 year old version of the SDQ is
scored in an identical way to the 4-17 year old version of the SDQ, and
we therefore suggest that you start by reading those instructions. The
only differences are:

-   The wording of two items on the 'conduct' scales is markedly
    different in the questionnaire for 2-4 year olds compared to the
    questionnaire for 4-17 (but the scoring stays the same). One further
    hyperactivity item is softened slightly in the 2-4 year old
    questionnaire. These three items are highlighted in Table 1.

-   Large population-based surveys in the UK suggest slightly different
    population norms for 2-4 year olds compared to older children. The
    banding of SDQ scores for the 2-4 year old version is shown in Table 3.  

**Total difficulties score**: This is generated by summing scores from
all the scales except the prosocial scale. The resultant score ranges
from 0 to 40, and is counted as missing if one of the 4 component scores
is missing.

don't sum: 1, 4, 9, 17, 20

reverse code: 7, 21, 25, 11, 14

**Assumptions:** used LAST follow-up if 2+ assessments exist; filtered
out NA's from follow-up date and positive outcome variable before
calculating %.

#### Cut off bands

We used the SDQ distribution data to propose the following banding of
SDQ scores for 2-4 year olds. We have sought cut-points such that around
80% of children are 'close to average', 12% 'slightly raised', 4% 'high'
and 4% 'very high' (or, for the prosocial scale, 80% are close to
average, 12% 'slightly lowered', 4% 'low' and 4% 'very low').

Similar cut-points were observed for parent SDQs collected in a smaller
American sample (N=307) of 2-4 year olds, and for parent SDQs collected
in the English 'Mental Health of Children And Young People, 2017' study.

|   | Close to average | Slightly raised (/slightly lowered) | High (/Low) | Very high (/very low) |
|----|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Parented completed SDQ total score | 0-12 | 13-15 | 16-18 | 19-40 |
| Teacher completed SDQ total score | 0-10 | 11-14 | 15-17 | 18-40 |

### 4-10 (Provider)

**Scoring:** The 25 items in the SDQ comprise 5 scales of 5 items each.
It is usually easiest to score all 5 scales first before working out the
total difficulties score. 'Somewhat True' is always scored as 1, but the
scoring of 'Not True' and 'Certainly True' varies with the item, as
shown below scale by scale. For each of the 5 scales the score can range
from 0 to 10 if all items were completed. These scores can be scaled up
pro-rata if at least 3 items were completed, e.g. a score of 4 based on
3 completed items can be scaled up to a score of 7 (6.67 rounded up) for
5 items.

**Total difficulties score**: This is generated by summing scores from
all the scales except the prosocial scale. The resultant score ranges
from 0 to 40, and is counted as missing of one of the 4 component scores
is missing.

don't sum: 1, 4, 9, 17, 20

reverse code: 7, 21, 25, 11, 14

**Assumptions:** used LAST follow-up if 2+ assessments exist; filtered
out NA's from follow-up date and positive outcome variable before
calculating %.

#### Cut off bands

|   | Close to average | Slightly raised (/slightly lowered) | High (/Low) | Very high (/very low) |
|----|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Parented completed SDQ total score | 0-13 | 14-16 | 17-19 | 20-40 |
| Teacher completed SDQ total score | 0-11 | 12-15 | 16-18 | 19-40 |
| Self completed SDQ total score | 0-14 | 15-17 | 18-19 | 20-40 |

### 11-17 (Provider)

It is usually easiest to score all 5 scales first before working out the

# Data quality checks

These counts are for review, not reporting.

```{r}
#| label: qa
qa_flow |>
  mutate(n = fmt_n_qa(n)) |>
  rename(Step = step, N = n) |>
  show_table("qa_sample_flow", caption = "Sample flow")
```

```{r}
#| label: export
export_long <- imap_dfr(EXPORT, function(tbl, id) {
  first <- names(tbl)[1]
  tbl |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character), row_order = row_number()) |>
    rename(row = all_of(first)) |>
    pivot_longer(-c(row, row_order), names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(table = id, row_header = first, .before = 1)
}) |>
  mutate(render_mode = RUN_MODE, suppress_n = SUPPRESS_N, .before = 1)

export_path <- file.path(cfg$output_dir, paste0(FILE_TAG, "_tables_", RUN_MODE, ".csv"))
write_csv(export_long, export_path, na = "")
```
